definitionEn: to successfully bring about or reach a desired result through effort
exampleSentence: Few teams achieve consensus on the first attempt at a design review.

definitionEn: to buy or obtain an asset, or to learn and develop a skill
exampleSentence: The company acquired a smaller competitor to expand its market share.

definitionEn: to have an influence on someone or something; to produce a change
exampleSentence: Sleep deprivation affects reaction time even after a single missed night.

definitionEn: suitable or proper in the circumstances
exampleSentence: The committee decided a written warning was the appropriate response.

definitionEn: a particular part or feature of a situation, idea, or problem
exampleSentence: The proposal addresses only the financial aspect of the merger, not the legal one.

definitionEn: to help someone by doing a share of the work or offering advice
exampleSentence: Graduate students assist faculty with grading and laboratory supervision.

definitionEn: a class or division of things regarded as having particular shared characteristics
exampleSentence: Survey responses were sorted into four broad categories before analysis.

definitionEn: a group of people living in the same place or sharing a particular characteristic
exampleSentence: The clinic was designed to serve the surrounding rural community.

definitionEn: consisting of many interconnected parts; not easy to understand or analyze
exampleSentence: The negotiations proved far more complex than either side had anticipated.

definitionEn: to bring something to an end, or to decide something after reasoning
exampleSentence: The report concludes that early intervention reduces long-term costs.

definitionEn: to organize and carry out a particular activity, or to behave in a particular way
exampleSentence: The team conducted the interviews over a period of six weeks.

definitionEn: following as a result or effect of something
exampleSentence: The consequent drop in demand forced the factory to cut its workforce.

definitionEn: to build or form something by putting parts together
exampleSentence: Researchers constructed a model to predict how the disease would spread.

definitionEn: to use up a resource, or to eat or drink something
exampleSentence: The new engine consumes almost thirty percent less fuel per mile.

definitionEn: the ability to obtain goods before payment based on trust, or public acknowledgment for an achievement
exampleSentence: The bank extended additional credit to help the firm cover payroll.

definitionEn: the customs, arts, and social institutions of a particular group or society
exampleSentence: Corporate culture proved harder to change than the org chart suggested.

definitionEn: to plan and produce something with a particular purpose or function in mind
exampleSentence: The survey was designed to minimize leading questions.

definitionEn: clearly different or separate; recognizably different in nature
exampleSentence: The survey identified three distinct groups of voters based on their priorities.

definitionEn: a basic or essential part of something
exampleSentence: Trust is a key element of any successful negotiation.

definitionEn: to form an idea of the amount, value, or quality of something after careful study
exampleSentence: Independent reviewers evaluated each proposal against the same five criteria.

definitionEn: a distinctive attribute or aspect of something
exampleSentence: The most striking feature of the data is how little it varies by region.

definitionEn: coming at the end of a series; not to be altered
exampleSentence: The final draft still needed a stronger conclusion.

definitionEn: to direct attention or effort toward a particular activity or subject
exampleSentence: The second half of the course focuses on statistical inference.

definitionEn: a marked effect or influence, or the action of one object forcefully hitting another
exampleSentence: The drought had a severe impact on regional grain production.

definitionEn: to establish or introduce a policy, practice, or procedure
exampleSentence: The board instituted a new review process after the audit.

definitionEn: to put money into financial schemes or property with the expectation of profit
exampleSentence: The fund invests primarily in early-stage renewable energy companies.

definitionEn: an individual article or unit, especially one included in a list or set
exampleSentence: Each item on the questionnaire was rated on a five-point scale.

definitionEn: to keep something in an existing state, or to assert something as true
exampleSentence: The author maintains that the earlier estimates were too conservative.

definitionEn: conforming to a standard; usual or expected
exampleSentence: Blood pressure returned to a normal range within two weeks of treatment.

definitionEn: to get or acquire something, typically through effort
exampleSentence: Permission to access the archive was difficult to obtain.

definitionEn: to take part in an activity or event
exampleSentence: Only volunteers who completed the screening could participate in the trial.

definitionEn: to become aware of something through the senses, or to interpret it in a certain way
exampleSentence: Participants perceived the second tone as louder, even though it was identical.

definitionEn: constructive and confident, or characterized by the presence of a quality or test result
exampleSentence: A positive test result triggered an automatic follow-up appointment.

definitionEn: having the capacity to develop into something in the future
exampleSentence: The drug showed potential benefits in early animal trials.

definitionEn: existing or occurring before something else in time or order
exampleSentence: The results replicate a pattern found in three previous studies.

definitionEn: of chief importance, or occurring first in a sequence or order
exampleSentence: The primary goal of the pilot program was to test enrollment procedures.

definitionEn: the scope of variation between limits, or a set of different things of the same general type
exampleSentence: Applicants came from a wide range of academic backgrounds.

definitionEn: an area or division, especially part of a country or the world, having definable characteristics
exampleSentence: Rainfall in the northern region was well below the seasonal average.

definitionEn: to control or maintain the rate of something, or to control it by rule or restriction
exampleSentence: A separate agency regulates the safety of imported food products.

definitionEn: closely connected or appropriate to the matter at hand
exampleSentence: Only the most relevant citations were kept in the final bibliography.

definitionEn: a stock or supply of materials, assets, or support that can be drawn on
exampleSentence: Limited resources forced the clinic to prioritize emergency cases.

definitionEn: to place a limit on something, or keep it within particular limits
exampleSentence: The new rule restricts access to the archive to registered researchers.

definitionEn: to obtain or achieve something, often with effort, or to make something safe
exampleSentence: The startup secured funding just before its cash reserves ran out.

definitionEn: to attempt to find or obtain something

definitionEn: to carefully choose something from a range of options

definitionEn: a plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim
exampleSentence: The firm revised its pricing strategy after losing market share.

definitionEn: a general examination of something, or an investigation of opinions via questionnaire
exampleSentence: The survey drew responses from over three thousand households.

definitionEn: a written or printed work regarded in terms of its content
exampleSentence: The exam asks students to compare two texts written a century apart.

definitionEn: a custom or belief passed down within a society or group
exampleSentence: The ceremony follows a tradition that dates back over two centuries.

definitionEn: to move something from one place, person, or situation to another
